candidate.tested_scope: Only the public ClickHouse SQL Playground / live demo route for querying ClickHouse-hosted GitHub events as a third-party corroboration path. Self-hosted ClickHouse, raw GH Archive HTTP archives, and other third-party indexes are outside this audit.

verified_points: The SQL Playground exposes a public ClickHouse instance and documents direct client access to sql-clickhouse.clickhouse.com with demo read-only credentials.
The public service is backed by a ClickHouse Cloud instance rather than static-file-only retrieval.
The service enforces query-complexity/resource restrictions and an IP-keyed quota of 60 queries per hour.
The published deployment description states a fixed three-node cluster of 30 vCPUs each at publication time.
The guide states that its queries execute against the live demo environment sql.clickhouse.com.
GitHub events are continuously loaded into the playground's GitHub database/table and queried interactively.
The route is therefore a searchable hosted database service, not a target-addressable static HTTP archive.

observations: The first-party ClickHouse sources support the worker's class-capability claim: the playground provides a live searchable GitHub-events dataset.
The first-party sources also directly support the worker's hosted-compute classification: the playground is served by ClickHouse Cloud and queries execute on that external service.

A material additional constraint is primary-source verified: the playground has an IP-keyed finite rate limit of 60 queries per hour. This is not a monthly/trial/paid quota, so it does not by itself instantiate the exact monthly-quota prohibition, but it is a real external-service quota/rate-limit that any recurrence-safe route must tolerate.
